title: bee onboard seeds .bee/config-sample.json into the host repo
action: Per D3: onboard writes .bee/config-sample.json into the host repo, create-if-missing, exactly like the existing create_runtime_file entries (plan.rs:391-401 list + apply.rs:260-272 content arms). Content comes from the bee repo's own .bee/config-sample.json embedded at compile time — include_str! from templates.rs (path relative to the source file; add a test asserting the embedded bytes parse as JSON and contain a "herding" key so a moved file breaks the build loudly, not silently). Never overwrite an existing file (same rule as the other runtime files). Extend the existing onboard tests' expected-plan fixtures where they enumerate created files. Note: this makes onboard emit one more file in fresh repos — additive, no reader change.

truths: Fresh-repo onboard writes .bee/config-sample.json; an existing file is never overwritten
The embedded sample is include_str! of the repo's own sample and a test asserts it parses and carries the herding key
